scope_note: All papers and systems enumerated in the user-supplied MAS.md were checked against primary papers, author-linked repositories, committed artifacts, and official releases where available. Third-party implementations are not labeled official.

papers.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
papers.supported_mechanism: Protocol, answer visibility, and agreement prompts alter answer revision; effects are strongly dataset- and prompt-dependent, and original debate is not a universal improvement.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Medical expertise creation through discussion; evidence exchange as the mediator; equal-budget superiority over independent sampling.
papers.implementation_finding: Round-robin, agreement-prompt, angel/devil/judge, and majority systems are implemented; early stopping is unfinished in one path.
papers.logs_status: Sixteen static result images and analysis/config artifacts; no raw per-case debate trajectories.
papers.transfer: Freeze independent first-round outputs and randomize later information reveal.
papers.do_not_transfer: Free debate, agreement as truth, or majority without correct-minority protection.

papers.title: MedAgents: Large Language Models as Collaborators for Zero-shot Medical Reasoning
papers.supported_mechanism: A structured sequence of domain gathering, independent analysis, synthesis, and consultation is associated with gains; removing irrelevant experts can improve performance, supporting relevance/noise gating.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Specialty persona as independent expertise, unanimity as correctness, or the individual effect of summary and consultation.
papers.implementation_finding: The loop revises until all experts answer YES up to a configurable maximum; repository temperature is zero while the paper reports 1.0.
papers.logs_status: No run logs or results; code, prompts, and a MedQA test file only.
papers.transfer: Independent proposal channels with provenance and relevance gates.
papers.do_not_transfer: Unanimity stopping or state-destructive summarization.

papers.title: Enhancing Diagnostic Capability with Multi-Agents Conversational Large Language Models
papers.supported_mechanism: The MAC bundle improves several candidate/list endpoints, while doctor count, rounds, and self-refinement are not monotonically beneficial and case-specific specialty assignment has no significant advantage.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Case-specific specialty assignment, supervisor reasoning, or conversation as the source of gain under an equal budget.
papers.implementation_finding: AutoGen group chat uses automatic speaker selection with doctor, supervisor, no-supervisor, and specialist-assignment variants.
papers.logs_status: No committed conversations, summaries, results, or run logs.
papers.transfer: Hypothesis to test: finite proposal diversity plus a deterministic contract checker, against equal-budget independent-union and no-chat controls.
papers.do_not_transfer: Long free discussion or a final supervisor that independently rediagnoses.

papers.title: MDAgents: An Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Medical Decision-Making
papers.supported_mechanism: Compute need not be fixed across cases; the route-plus-compute bundle improves aggregate results in the reported setting.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Subjective difficulty as a calibrated treatment-effect router; separate effects of route, budget, RAG, moderator, and personas.
papers.implementation_finding: Public code maps several GPT-4/4o variants to gpt-4o-mini, hard-codes other models, discards compiled advanced-team reports in the final path, and does not implement the full paper bundle.
papers.logs_status: No data, results, logs, or complete experiment configuration.
papers.transfer: Conditional compute, but route observable disputed edges rather than case-level complexity.
papers.do_not_transfer: A free LLM complexity router or paper-level model labels trusted without call-path audit.

papers.title: Model Confrontation and Collaboration: A Debate Intelligence Framework for Enhancing Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.supported_mechanism: Initial disagreement identifies a subset where critique and revision can rescue errors, while persuasion and suppression also create initial-correct-to-final-wrong failures.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Conversation versus static heterogeneous aggregation, vendor diversity versus model strength, or evidence rather than order/authority as the mediator.
papers.implementation_finding: Sequential GPT-to-Qwen-to-DeepSeek revision checks consensus after each update; consensus filters parse failures and can fail open; final tie handling is brittle.
papers.logs_status: 2,865 committed case text logs: MedQA 1,273; PubMedQA 500; six MMLU subsets 1,089; LFQ 3. Full initial answers, critiques, revisions, consensus, and correctness are present, but only one visible run and no aggregate result file.
papers.transfer: Observable disagreement gating, new-claim yield, harmful persuasion, and suppression audit.
papers.do_not_transfer: Sequential free confrontation, majority truth, or parse-failure consensus.

papers.title: Do Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent LLMs Improve Clinical Diagnosis?
papers.supported_mechanism: Different vendors expose partially non-overlapping candidate sets; in this mixed bundle's overlap audit, small gains in some datasets coexist with losses of previously correct cases.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Heterogeneous conversation versus independent heterogeneous outputs plus deterministic fusion; robust superiority on small DA/MME samples.
papers.implementation_finding: Per-vendor agents and round-robin fusion are present; RareBench uses a Gemini supervisor where the paper generally states o4, and result naming can mislabel provenance.
papers.logs_status: No committed raw trajectories or result files.
papers.transfer: Measure claim/error decorrelation directly and compare against no-chat heterogeneous ensembles.
papers.do_not_transfer: Vendor count or role label as a diversity objective.

papers.title: MedLA: A Logic-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Complex Medical Reasoning with Large Language Models
papers.supported_mechanism: Localizing disagreement to propositions and revising low-confidence nodes is a plausible and bundle-supported alternative to whole-opinion debate.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Syllogism truth, independent contributions of logic/credibility/revision, or the paper architecture in the public code.
papers.implementation_finding: Current code lacks the paper's Premise, Decompose, Credibility, and tree-merge architecture; it randomly keeps one representative per unique answer and reuses a stale initial logic report. The CLI has reproducibility defects.
papers.logs_status: Eleven Plotly/Sankey HTML visualizations; no W&B history, aggregate metrics, config, or complete run logs.
papers.transfer: Typed, source-bound candidate-relative claims and localized edge revision.
papers.do_not_transfer: Generated premises treated as facts or logical-tree form treated as validity.

papers.title: Let LLMs Judge Each Other: Multi-Agent Peer-Reviewed Reasoning for Medical Question Answering
papers.supported_mechanism: The reported reviewer-score averaging selector is higher than the repository's flawed majority baseline for selected model compositions; it operates on frozen generated candidates.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Rationale quality versus a reviewer independently knowing the answer; post-hoc best combination as a deployable configuration.
papers.implementation_finding: All reviewer-by-candidate scores are averaged; ties select the first candidate. Majority ties are accidentally alphabetic, default rubric/parser paths differ from the paper, and 26 combinations are swept on test.
papers.logs_status: No README, requirements, dataset, results, configs, or run logs.
papers.transfer: Mirrored frozen pair comparison after answer-only and rationale-shuffle calibration.
papers.do_not_transfer: Mean free-rationale self-review score as a posterior probability.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Reasoning with Consistency Verification Improves Uncertainty Calibration in Medical MCQA
papers.supported_mechanism: Multiplying overconfident self-reports by a consistency penalty shrinks confidence and lowers all four ECE point estimates; paper bootstrap intervals separate C4 from C1 in three of four sets, while accuracy and AUROC do not consistently improve.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Consistency as a stable per-case correctness detector, specialty persona diversity, or hard verification veto.
papers.implementation_finding: Four greedy same-model specialty initial answers are followed by fixed-seed temperature-sampled verification; S=C0*(1-I), and answer fusion is the sum of supporter S-scores.
papers.logs_status: 2,800 main per-case config records and 3,200 per-specialist records reproduce aggregate metrics. C2 stores final S_score but not I; C4 omits per-specialist S, complete rationales, verification questions/answers, and fusion traces. Current C3-saving code postdates the committed main artifact schema.
papers.transfer: Soft risk feature, abstention, and calibration reporting.
papers.do_not_transfer: Consistency as evidence truth, likelihood, or candidate deletion.

papers.title: Clinical Counterfactual Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.supported_mechanism: The entire counterfactual-editing pathway has a small-sample bundle contribution within its multi-agent scaffold.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Its public absolute label-shift score as a fixed-candidate causal effect; specialist discussion as the mediator.
papers.implementation_finding: Candidate sets and generated labels are not frozen, absolute rather than signed changes are scored, SIP can fail open, and confidence is length-sensitive/free-text dependent.
papers.logs_status: Fully audited in the prior counterfactual report; not re-run here.
papers.transfer: Validity-gated, fixed-candidate, signed disputed-edge counterfactual audit.
papers.do_not_transfer: Counterfactual text as fact, absolute label shift, or free candidate substitution.

papers.title: MEDDxAgent: A Unified Modular Agent Framework for Explainable Automatic Differential Diagnosis
papers.supported_mechanism: Fixed action coverage and explicit DDx state updates often beat a free router. New observations and label-bearing nearest examples are simultaneous interventions whose contributions are not separated; logs expose a strong label prior.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Three-agent collaboration under fixed information/call budget, or RAG versus history versus diagnosis as separate mediators.
papers.implementation_finding: DDxDriver, fixed/open schedules, patient simulator, history, diagnosis, and search RAG are present; one conditional RAG path is not actually honored and the MedRAG class is intentionally unusable.
papers.logs_status: Two patient logs plus two-case results/config. Retrieved few-shot examples expose the same ground-truth pathology labels; no full experiment logs.
papers.transfer: Typed case state, fixed or observable-trigger scheduling, and gap-to-approved-query.
papers.do_not_transfer: Synthetic patient answers, unrestricted router, or label-bearing neighbors as collaboration evidence.

papers.title: MeDxAgent: Multi-Agent Consultation for Interactive Medical Diagnosis
papers.supported_mechanism: Delaying diagnosis-conditioned questioning until hypotheses mature strongly improves results; candidate-blind case summarization has an isolated positive contribution, while other modules interact non-additively.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Individual specialist/KG/gap-agent effects, calibrated confidence stopping, or root-complete correctness.
papers.implementation_finding: Microsoft Research states code and data will be released upon publication; no author/Microsoft official repository was found as of the research date.
papers.logs_status: No official code or logs available.
papers.transfer: Candidate-blind state builder, delayed exploitation gate, and typed gap output.
papers.do_not_transfer: Early candidate-conditioned questioning or persona ensemble by default.

papers.title: Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models
papers.family: functional operators and cost-aware sequential diagnosis
papers.supported_mechanism: A single model acting as hypothesis, test choice, challenger, stewardship, and checklist operators can move the test-cost Pareto frontier; no-budget accuracy gains for strong models are not consistently significant.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Individual operator effects or validity of synthetic Gatekeeper findings as clinical observations.
papers.implementation_finding: No author/Microsoft official repository was found; a third-party Swarm implementation was explicitly excluded.
papers.logs_status: No official code or logs available.
papers.transfer: Top-pair challenger, value-of-information proposal, stewardship gate, and schema checklist as sequential operators.
papers.do_not_transfer: Synthetic tests, patient findings, or simulator reward into a static complete-vignette task.

papers.title: ClinicalAgents: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Clinical Decision Making with Dual-Memory
papers.supported_mechanism: Typed working state, action validity, gap detection, snapshots, and rollback contribute within the bundle; diagnostic gains over the strongest MAS comparator are small.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Classic MCTS exploration, working-memory main effect, or LLM confidence/reward as evidence truth.
papers.implementation_finding: The search score is Q plus lambda times an LLM prior without visit-dependent exploration; Top-K actions receive equal rollouts and benchmark ground truth materializes tests. Required modules and dependencies are missing.
papers.logs_status: No data, configs, results, or run logs; public commit cannot reproduce the experiments.
papers.transfer: Immutable snapshots, deterministic action validation, gap ledger, and bounded rollback.
papers.do_not_transfer: Model-simulated future evidence or self-confidence reward.

papers.title: MDTeamGPT: Mitigating Context Collapse and Enabling Self-Evolution in Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.supported_mechanism: Structured residual context and a lead synthesizer have a positive interaction; the largest gain comes from outcome-supervised answer-bearing retrieval memory.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Residual compression alone, unsupervised self-evolution, specialty roles, or leakage-safe transfer.
papers.implementation_finding: The demo retrieves KB before round one and exposes it to specialists, contrary to the paper's post-round-one injection; default retrieval k also differs, and the safety reviewer only sees the lead summary.
papers.logs_status: Eight code/demo files; no benchmark, KB, results, configs, or logs.
papers.transfer: Immutable multi-channel residual views only in VE-MAS v1.
papers.proposed_hypothesis: Answer-stripped success/error policy memory could be studied later under a separate preregistration, outcome-time split, and leakage audit; it is not a supported v1 transfer.
papers.do_not_transfer: Answer-bearing cross-case memory or summary as sole state.

papers.title: MedAgentBoard: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration with Conventional Methods for Diverse Medical Tasks
papers.supported_mechanism: MAS value is task-conditional; strong single or conventional methods often win, while workflow completeness gains bundle tools, code execution, state, and extra calls.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Persona discussion as the workflow mediator or a universal MAS advantage.
papers.implementation_finding: Benchmark runners and a separate workflow repository are available; the MC answer parser can map verbose text to A by substring and corrupt exact reported values.
papers.logs_status: Official Drive archive is 2,005,920,088 compressed bytes, 22,150 entries, about 3.43GB unpacked; main logs include 13,847 QA, 2,000 lay-summary, and 600 released EHR cases with case_history, but no per-case token usage.
papers.transfer: Task-conditional selection and strong single/conventional compute-matched baselines.
papers.do_not_transfer: Cross-task average as proof that a collaboration mechanism works.

papers.title: MedAgentAudit: Diagnosing and Quantifying Collaborative Failure Modes in Medical Multi-Agent Systems
papers.supported_mechanism: Correct-minority suppression, authority bias, repetition, unresolved conflict, and synthesis failures occur at material observed rates and can be audited with a structured taxonomy.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: Causal effect of preserving minority evidence, round number on authority bias, or post-hoc best framework selection as a deployable gain.
papers.implementation_finding: Current audit agents, framework hooks, statistics, and official release schemas are inspectable; older KEU/M1-M4 code belongs to a deprecated repository and is not quantified in the current paper.
papers.logs_status: Official release tag 5e964353e4c88e7b409d67f4736b39cdd1784695: 36 source JSONL/3,600 cases; 144 audit JSONL/14,370 valid; 24 single JSONL/2,395; extracted open-coding 35 files/677; audit-human 20/400; shared open-coding-human 33/330; invalid 6/27. The paper says 360 shared open-coding cases, whereas release/supplement material yields 330. Rich case_history and 10-mode audit fields are present.
papers.transfer: Interventional correct-minority survival, harmful persuasion, evidence retention, and redundant-call metrics.
papers.do_not_transfer: Observed failure frequency as a causal treatment effect.

papers.title: Grounding Large Language Models in Clinical Diagnostics
papers.family: dynamic clinical workflow and capability-limit audit
papers.supported_mechanism: Multi-doctor and critic effects are backbone-dependent; three GPT-4o-mini doctors give a small gain, whereas the same protocols significantly harm Qwen2.5-72B.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: A general MAS effect, critic benefit, or persuasion mediator under matched compute.
papers.implementation_finding: Round-robin multi-doctor and doctor-critic-provider workflows are implemented with up to 50 rounds per stage.
papers.logs_status: 2,021 public benchmark case directories; 13,141 ZIP entries and 10,142 payload files after excluding __MACOSX. No generated runs, results, or interaction logs; 2,400 MIMIC emergency cases are not public.
papers.transfer: A capability gate: architecture cannot manufacture missing procedural competence or absent candidates.
papers.do_not_transfer: Interactive workflow scores as a static selector endpoint.

papers.title: AgentRx: A Benchmark Study of LLM Agents for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks
papers.supported_mechanism: Results are consistent with a bundle-level loss when modalities are partitioned and then combined by arithmetic/free-text fusion; Qwen has correlated initial outputs before peer exposure, while MedGemma often follows the initial majority after exposure.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: The cross-modal interaction mediator separate from information partition, prompt, call graph, and aggregation; universal single-agent superiority under matched compute.
papers.implementation_finding: Unimodal majority averages probabilities; debate and Traj-CoA are implemented, but saved results generally retain final predictions rather than full peer reasoning.
papers.logs_status: 321 tracked files and extraction resources; no paper outputs, results, or interaction traces.
papers.transfer: Preserve raw shared facts and audit cross-fact/cross-modality interactions before decomposition.
papers.do_not_transfer: Independent summaries as a substitute for the shared evidence ledger.

papers.title: MedicalAgentsBench for Complex Medical Reasoning
papers.family: hard-set benchmark of internalized and externalized reasoning
papers.supported_mechanism: Some model-method bundles improve hard-set accuracy, but gains are small versus strong single reasoning and expensive; other backbones favor single/self-refine methods.
papers.mechanism_not_identified: The reported o3 MDAgents score as multi-agent collaboration, because 98.21 percent of released cases do not enter a multi-agent branch, although the basic path still makes about eight calls.
papers.implementation_finding: The paper states standardized two-round three-role MDAgents, while code uses adaptive difficulty; 2,476 of 2,521 o3 cases are basic, with only 8 intermediate and 37 advanced. Basic still makes multiple calls.
papers.logs_status: Main output: 1,385 JSON, 385,204 records, about 1.06GB; MDAgents 108 JSON/10,219 records; MedAgents 118/11,067; baseline CSV 792 rows; paper-hard predictions 75,764. Headline MedAgents/MDAgents outputs omit agent opinions and rounds.
papers.transfer: Hard-set, cost, latency, and strong single-method controls; audit the executed branch rather than the method label.
papers.do_not_transfer: Leaderboard method names as proof that collaboration executed or caused the result.
